pages.text: Cast iron is the metal of your first heavy machines: the coke oven, the blast stove, cast iron pipes and tanks.

$(l)Making it$()$(br)Put a $(item)mechanical press$() over a $(item)basin$(), with a lit $(item)blaze burner$() under the basin. Drop in $(item)1 iron ingot + 1 coal$(): the press compacts them into $(item)1 cast iron ingot$(). The recipe needs heat, a cold basin does nothing.
Charcoal does not work here, it must be coal. Crushing lignite is a good source of extra coal.$(br2)$(l)Storage and shapes$()$(li)9 cast iron nuggets make an ingot, and an ingot gives 9 nuggets back.
$(li)9 ingots make a $(item)block of cast iron$(), which the blast furnace output needs.$(li)Press an ingot with a mechanical press on a depot or a belt for a $(item)cast iron sheet$().
Automate it early: a hopper or funnel feeding iron and coal into the heated basin, and a second press making sheets, will cover the whole chapter.
